extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for recipients to design and operate Title IX grievance procedures, including protections for participants, appeals, notice, sanctions, and special rules for student-employees. Focuses on procedural safeguards to ensure prompt, equitable, and non-discriminatory resolution of sex discrimination and sex‑based harassment complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disciplining based solely on grievance outcome (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not discipline a party, witness, or other participant based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(h)(5) preserves a recipient's discretion to discipline those who make false statements (including materially false statements made in bad faith) only if there is evidence independent of, or in addition to, the outcome of the Title IX grievance proceeding. The provision applies to anyone who participates in grievance procedures (not just complainants) and is only applicable after a determination whether sex discrimination occurred. It does not pertain to factfinding and does not prohibit decisionmakers from considering credibility during the grievance process. Threatening or instituting disciplinary proceedings under circumstances outlined in §106.71 could still constitute retaliation under that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of evidence developed in Title IX processes for separate disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence developed during the Title IX grievance process may be used in a separate disciplinary process addressing false statements, provided the disciplinary charge is not based solely on the grievance outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department clarifies that using evidence from the grievance process in independent disciplinary proceedings is permissible so long as there is independent evidence beyond the outcome. The Department declines to mandate how recipients structure their non-Title IX disciplinary processes for false statements (e.g., requiring policies, mandatory discipline, or nondisclosure agreements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from collateral discipline for consensual sexual activity (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not impose collateral discipline based solely on a determination whether sex discrimination occurred for consensual sexual conduct that would deter participation in grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some institutions have codes prohibiting consensual sexual conduct, inclusion of consensual sexual activity in §106.45(h)(5) removes a potential barrier to participation and fosters equitable grievance processes. The Department rejects arguments that this language is unnecessary and explains the inclusion is intended to promote full and accurate fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals must be at least as available as in comparable proceedings (§106.45(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to an appeal of a dismissal consistent with §106.45(d)(3), a recipient must offer an appeal process to parties that is, at minimum, the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complaints of sex-based harassment involving a postsecondary student, a postsecondary institution must also offer an appeal on the bases set out in §106.46(i)(1). Recipients retain discretion to offer appeals in other cases but must not exercise that discretion arbitrarily. The regulations do not prescribe specific categories of appeals or a specific timeframe for appeal, but any adopted appeal process must apply equally to the parties and be implemented within a recipient's reasonably prompt timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional grievance provisions must apply equally to the parties (§106.45(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional provisions a recipient adopts as part of its grievance procedures must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department retains the term 'equally' rather than 'equitably'—meaning additional provisions must be available to both parties even if implementation differs based on individual needs (e.g., disability accommodations or interpreters provided to only the party who needs them still satisfies equality). Recipients may use shared governance or collective bargaining to adopt additional procedures, and employee-specific rights under such agreements may differ from non-employee parties so long as the requirement of equal opportunity to receive additional provisions is met. If a recipient adopts grievance procedures that apply to some but not all complaints, it must articulate consistent principles for determining applicability (§106.45(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: List or describe range of supportive measures and disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must list, or describe the range of, supportive measures available to complainants and respondents and the possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies that may be imposed following a determination that sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule revised language to require recipients to 'List, or describe the range of' possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies. Recipients may impose only those disciplinary sanctions that are set forth in their list or range, including sanctions imposed after a respondent has graduated. The Department declines to prescribe specific sanctions, recognizing variation across recipient types, populations, and applicable law. Title IX Coordinators do not have authority to bring civil or criminal charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Clery Act for sanctions lists
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Clery Act applies to a recipient, the Clery Act's required list of sanctions satisfies §106.45(l)(2), but recipients must supplement the list for Title IX-related sanctions not covered by Clery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clery Act lists cover certain crimes (rape, domestic violence, etc.) and satisfy §106.45(l)(2) for those matters; however, §106.45(l) applies to a broader set of recipients (including K-12) and types of conduct (e.g., quid pro quo, hostile environment) so recipients must add to Clery lists if they intend to impose other types of sanctions for sex-based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-employee fact-specific inquiry (§106.46(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party is both a student and an employee, a postsecondary institution must conduct a fact-specific inquiry to determine whether §106.46 applies, considering whether the party's primary relationship is to receive an education or whether the alleged harassment occurred during education-related activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfying either factor is sufficient (but not required) to apply §106.46; institutions may consider additional factors and weigh them at their discretion. If §106.46 does not apply, the institution must comply with §106.45. Institutions remain able to impose adverse employment actions as disciplinary sanctions following a Title IX determination, may place student-employee respondents on administrative leave during grievance proceedings (§106.44(i)), and need not be limited to one resolution process in their rules (but a given complaint will be governed by one set of Title IX grievance procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations must include presumption of non-responsibility (§106.46(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice of allegations must include a statement that the respondent is presumed not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination whether sex-based harassment occurred is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is part of ensuring fairness and reliable outcomes. Notice of allegations must be provided to parties whose identities are known (both complainants and respondents). The Department also clarifies that allowing respondents time to prepare for interviews is fair and consistent with Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present evidence to trained, impartial decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must have the opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to trained, impartial decisionmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may have more than one decisionmaker; references to 'a' decisionmaker are not meant to limit this. Written notice of allegations must assure parties they will have an opportunity to present evidence to the decisionmakers assigned to their case. Decisionmakers must be trained and free from bias or conflicts of interest (see related §106.45 provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible delayed notice for legitimate safety concerns (§106.46(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may delay providing notice of allegations to a respondent if the recipient takes steps to address legitimate safety concerns that would arise from immediate notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department allows delayed notice to protect safety (e.g., protecting complainants alleging dating/domestic violence). Commenters asked for more specificity (what qualifies as 'legitimate concern for safety,' timeframes, documentation); the Department accepts the provision but did not mandate specific timeframes, instead allowing recipients discretion while noting the need to document the justification for any delay.
